sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability, funding and tradeability. This is a cyclical coke manufacturer with trading exposure, not an evidence-backed compounder. A domestic policy tailwind and a genuine RINL order create recovery possibilities, but they do not outweigh declining core manufacturing, weak incremental returns and poor cash conversion.

The decisive distinction is between reported cash and usable liquidity. At 31 March 2026, ₹5.3933 crore cash included ₹4.1978 crore earmarked IPO money and ₹1.1207 crore LC margin. Only ₹0.0748 crore remains after those labels. At the same date, one related-party receivable was ₹20.0108 crore, almost half total receivables. Recoverability and the bridge from sales/advances to that balance need evidence, not an assumed write-off or collection.

BQS and IAS are NS because balance-sheet/current-financing and price/implementation inputs are materially missing. GQS is 2.4/10, with the persistent weak-cash/capital-return ceiling of 5 explicitly applicable. No factor is filled with 5 merely to complete a score. Ordinary returns and entry prices are suppressed. Hypothetical prefunded rescue cases are diagnostic only. Positive audit findings and the absence of a current-year default are preserved; neither the 2018 OTS nor an issuer-noncooperation rating is called a current default.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Research cutoff 20 October 2026; intended market reference 19 October 2026. Investment horizon 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 is 1,826 days, divided by 365.25. The equity hurdle is nominal INR 15% before personal taxes, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. ₹500,000 is an illustrative implementation position, not an allocation recommendation.

The security is BSE SME 544510, NCML, ISIN INE346R01013, CIN L23101OR2003PLC007061. The interoperability master usesNCML$ and SM and confirms 1,600 share lot and 24,927,000 issued shares. This does not make the company NSE-listed. No authenticated BSE cutoff close was obtained; ₹118.50 is an explicitly assumed scenario price. Rolling secondary snapshots and search snippets are not official historical price evidence.

Historical statements have Medium confidence: full audited/restated originals support calculations, but connected receivables and several disclosure inconsistencies remain material. Growth decomposition is Medium, with FY26 tonnes/prices unavailable. Incremental capital calculations are Medium, supported by comparable consolidated accounts and two-sided bridges, not private project IRRs. Current funding and valuation inputs are Low. Governance is Medium, reflecting documented concerns plus favourable counterevidence. G1 is Conditional, G2/G3/G4 are Hold. All numerical ranking flags are false, including the otherwise computable GQS, because the reliability hold is relevant to comparison.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 primitive factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 1, DUR 5, CAP 3, CASH 1, BAL NS, EXEC 4, EARN 3, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. Scores represent bounded judgments, not calibrated probabilities. Every factor retains its evidence, contrary fact and upgrade/downgrade trigger in the embedded audit.

BQS uses the exact v3 weights 20/20/12/10/12/10/8/8%. Its known weighted sum is 3.00 at 92% coverage. The mathematical missing-data bound is 3.08–3.80; BQS remains NS, not the bound midpoint. GQS uses 40/20/15/15/10% for REV/DUR/EARN/CAP/CASH. Raw and final GQS are 2.40, displayed 2.4. CAP 3 and CASH 1 reflect persistent poor realised economics, so the ceiling 5 applies even though it is nonbinding here.

IAS reuses final unrounded BQS at 25%, then R 35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10%. With only D scored, known contribution is 0.60, coverage 20%, and the mathematical bound 1.40–8.60 is not a ranking. IAS remains NS. No governance override is applied at GOV 4: the evidence does not yet establish severe abusive conduct. Moving GOV to 3 on sufficient adverse evidence would trigger the framework override and Avoid—governance, while missing aggregates stay NS. One-point GOV/MOAT sensitivities are disclosed rather than treating small differences as precise rankings.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Nilachal has operated since 2003 and manufactures low-ash metallurgical coke and coke fines for steel, ferroalloy and foundry-related buyers, alongside coal/coke trading. The consolidated perimeter includes virtually wholly owned Nilachal Coffee & Agro Estate. That subsidiary is not a material acquisition-driven revenue engine. The historical business is physical and working-capital intensive: coking-coal procurement, conversion, inventory, customer qualification and collection are the economic chain.

The prospectus capacity base was 102,000 TPA: 60,000 owned Odisha capacity,18,000 leased Vizag and 24,000 Dhamra tolling. FY23/24/25 production 65,863/62,741/49,852 tonnes implies 64.57%/61.51%/48.87% utilisation on that definition. A later consent permits owned capacity to increase to 108,000 TPA through two 24,000 TPA batteries. Prospectus expansion references 34,400 TPA, with a smaller technical figure elsewhere. These are not interchangeable definitions and none proves commissioning or utilisation.

FY26 revenue ₹200.3966 crore was nearly flat versus ₹201.5120 crore in FY25, but its composition deteriorated. Manufacturing coke/fines/other revenue was about ₹141.5347 crore, while trading contributed ₹58.8620 crore against virtually none in FY25. Trading gross contribution was only about ₹0.2541 crore before shared overhead. Core manufacturing sales fell about 31%. FY26 tonnes and realised prices were not verified, so the model transparently uses separate manufacturing-volume/price and trading-growth assumptions rather than inventing a tonnage bridge.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is delivered cost and operating access, not a brand moat. Odisha proximity to coal/ports/customers, established ovens and repeat qualification can reduce logistics friction. The mechanism would be a sustained delivered-cost gap that survives commodity cycles. Evidence currently establishes location and operating history, not a quantified structural cost lead or contractual customer lock-in. A capable domestic coke producer or imported alternative can compete if specifications and landed price are acceptable.

The final anti-dumping measure offers protection against specified imports, but its exclusions matter for Nilachal’s actual customers. Ultra-low-phosphorus coke at or below 0.030% phosphorus and specified small sizes for actual-user ferroalloys, semi/soft coke and specified 20–40 mm coke for small pig-iron furnaces are excluded. The final notification runs for five years from the provisional 31 December 2025 imposition, unless earlier amended or revoked. Scheduled protection therefore ends around December 2030, before the model’s 20 October 2031 terminal date. Renewal is not assumed; terminal margins remain analytical scenarios, with lower-margin downside already tested. Therefore a generic statement that all relevant imports are blocked indefinitely would overstate addressable protection. DGTR records also show domestic alternatives, including Jindal, Saurashtra and VISA-related producers, and customer qualification negotiations. These are stronger competitive checks than a listed-peer P/E table.

Buyer concentration weakens bargaining power: FY25 top five customers were 86.28% of sales, top ten 98.83%, largest 28.33%. The largest supplier represented 53.06% of purchases and top five 87.86%. Neither customer names nor certifications prove pricing power. A stronger moat case requires through-cycle superior delivered margins, lower cash capital per tonne, retention across price shocks and demonstrable entry/qualification barriers. MOAT 4 recognises operating access without awarding a durable franchise premium.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The declared core comparison is FY22–FY26, four elapsed years, with FY21 retained as five-year context rather than silently omitted. FY22–26 sales CAGR is 0.15%; operating value-added CAGR is about −0.36%, operating EBIT CAGR 4.39% and reported PAT CAGR −5.13%. On a consistent 25% tax basis excluding other income, normalised PAT grew 5.36% and current-share-denominator normalised EPS grew 2.50% annually; earlier unusually low taxes make reported PAT growth look weaker than this operating comparison. The more recent FY23–26 sales CAGR is −9.03%. Production FY23–25 declined at about 13% annually. Annual absolute revenue additions and complete financial rows are embedded.

The framework nominal growth anchor is 2 for 0–5% CAGR. A one-point downward trajectory adjustment yields REV 1 because recent revenue and volumes decline, while the longer-window value-added check does not support a hidden high-growth business. The contextual FY21–26 five-year revenue CAGR is 11.60%. The FY21 base was affected by the pandemic and is disclosed separately, not used selectively to manufacture an attractive growth rate. No material acquisition contribution was identified; the coffee subsidiary does not explain consolidated scaling.

FY26 reported stability is not organic manufacturing stability: a substantial low-margin trading line replaced lost manufacturing revenue. Higher gross turnover from trading can consume working capital without comparable value creation. The April 2026 RINL purchase order of ₹35.11048 crore is positive commercial evidence, but disclosed in May and partly linked to temporary IPO working-capital use. Without order execution, cancellation, price-escalation, margin and collection details, it cannot simply be added to FY26 revenue or treated as unexecuted multi-year backlog.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Incremental returns, not capacity announcements, are the central test. Invested capital is reconciled from equity plus interest-bearing debt less cash and investments, adding back LC security because it is operating capital. Unused IPO cash is excluded as uninvested. Supplier/capital advances and related loans remain capital allocated once; shifting them into PPE does not create fresh investment. An independently constructed asset-minus-operating-liability side reconciles within rounding, and annual component bridges explain the change.

Using a standard 25% operating tax assumption, the FY22–26 incremental NOPAT/IC proxy is about 1.93%, FY23–26 about 1.25%, and FY24–26 about −2.05%. These are accounting allocation proxies, not project IRRs. FY21–26 context is also embedded. Earlier CSR costs charged directly to reserves rather than P&L are separately sensitised. The direct-reserve CSR sensitivity raises the FY22–26 proxy to 2.32% and the contextual FY21–26 proxy to 6.05%. Even that adjustment does not establish returns near the diagnostic 12–16% nominal INR capital-cost range. Some expansion capital is immature, so a lagged improvement could change the assessment; current ROCE alone cannot do so.

The bear/base/bull model separates manufacturing growth from low-margin trading, retains maintenance capex beyond the IPO period and links incremental working capital to revenue. It does not release existing related receivables, supplier advances or GST credits optimistically. Capacity consent and demand access create a runway, but the usable runway depends on funded commissioning, qualification, actual tonnes and collections. CAP 3 and CASH 1 therefore constrain growth quality rather than treating demand or a small market capitalisation as value creation.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held about 73.52% after the IPO, principally Kajal Fashion and the managing promoter. The offer raised ₹22.10 crore fresh capital for the company, while ₹34 crore OFS benefited the selling shareholder. These flows are kept separate. Promoter remuneration of about ₹1.08 crore is roughly 10% of FY26 PAT; remuneration alone is not evidence of abuse, but minority alignment must be tested alongside capital deployment and connected funding.

The strongest concern is documentary inconsistency, not an accusation of fraud. The complete IPO auditor certificate says temporary working-capital use of ₹3.4235 crore resulted in a deviation from prospectus objects. The issuer’s cover says N.A., and annual disclosures say no deviation. Management explains inventory/liquidity needs for business, including the RINL order. Capital utilisation ₹8.8718 crore includes vendor advances. The certificate’s net proceeds/expense bridge differs from annual cashflow/equity accounting by ₹1.1428 crore. These require reconciliation and disclosure correction.

Om Avi Carbon’s ₹20.0108 crore receivable is large relative to disclosed related sales and the prior advance balance; pricing, settlement and recoverability are open. A separate ₹0.4354 crore loan and ₹5.20 crore guarantee expand exposure but are not all simultaneous liabilities. Kajal’s ₹20.4337 crore loan can support liquidity, yet terms matter. Full audit/IFC/audit-trail positives and no current-year default are meaningful contrary evidence. Current October pledge status is not independently established; no blanket pledge-free claim is made. GOV 4 is a cautious stewardship assessment, not the severe governance override.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 reported CFO was −₹32.0062 crore. The cashflow statement includes −₹1.2007 crore short-term borrowing movement within operating cash; removing that financing classification gives −₹30.8055 crore after interest. Interest is already inside FY26 operating profit/PAT and is not added back a second time. The ₹26.6803 crore advance absorption is not all customer working capital: supplier advances ₹36.1871 crore, including capital-related amounts, and GST credits ₹10.7913 crore are substantial. Receivables increased ₹12.1583 crore and inventory ₹4.9363 crore. Capital-advance reclassification can change CFO presentation but not cash after total reinvestment.

FY25 restated CFO ₹2.7061 crore differs from the latest comparative −₹2.4606 crore chiefly because of interest, borrowing and advance classifications. The complete reconciliation is embedded; this is not automatically missing cash. FY22 original cash includes LC deposits and small investments, explaining the restated opening difference. FY21/22 CSR ₹0.3208142/₹0.424545 crore was directly charged to reserves, explaining part of the equity/PAT bridge and requiring earnings sensitivity.

Across FY22–26, reported CFO totals −₹22.5337 crore against ₹68.1960 crore PAT. Financing-neutral post-interest CFO totals −₹35.6737 crore; disclosed cash-capex FCF is still weaker. Four consecutive FY23–26 years are negative on that cash basis. Full audits are unmodified and bank returns reconcile, but unreported GSTR 1 sales ₹1.995 crore, an unupdated gratuity valuation and obvious IPO/listing/date contradictions remain unresolved. No current default, fraud or statutory arrears beyond six months was reported in CARO. A clean main opinion is neither ignored nor treated as proof that every annexure is clean.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
No ordinary fair-value or expected-return conclusion is available: both an authenticated cutoff price and current funding are missing. At the explicitly assumed ₹118.50 and 24.927 million shares, scenario equity value is ₹295.385 crore and enterprise value about ₹333.886 crore after only apparently free cash. Cross-checks are about 28.0 times reported earnings,27.5 times 25%-tax normalised earnings,15.6 times operating EBITDA and 2.71 times book. Book value is not liquidation support when it includes connected receivables, advances and tax credits. Prospectus peer multiples are not used as a valuation anchor.

The primary diagnostic is a monthly operating/funding model from 31 March 2026 to 20 October 2031, with a distinct 20 October 2026 entry snapshot and annual rollups. Current interest, taxes, old tax/statutory/gratuity balances, recurring maintenance/growth capex, eligible IPO uses and optional repayments/calls are reconciled once. IPO earmarks fund only eligible capex;LC cash is not free. All cases test opening, pre-entry and conservative pre-generation interval troughs. A negative modeled balance is a funding requirement, never an automatic loan plug or evidence of actual default.

The baseline reserve is ₹0.5 crore, sensitised from zero to ₹1 crore. Any breach suppresses non-rescue conditional returns and entry prices. Rescue cases issue whole shares before all modeled uses, at 30% discount with 3% fees; gross, fees, net and dilution reconcile. They are hypothetical, not known financing or an R score. Complete growth/multiple, WC/capex, reserve/related-loan and 12/15/18% hurdle grids are embedded. Reverse expectations use finite scans and verified bracket crossings; no endpoint is labelled a solution.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-loss risk is High. The linked failure path is customer or commodity-price weakness, lower oven utilisation, weaker margins, slow connected/customer collections, additional inventory/supplier funding, then adverse refinancing or equity issuance. A temporary quotation decline is not the same as impairment, but an unrecoverable related balance or forced deeply discounted recapitalisation can permanently reduce per-share claims.

The bear model lowers manufacturing volume and price 2% each annually, trading 5%, manufacturing EBITDA margin to 11%, raises incremental WC to 70% of revenue growth, increases remaining project spend, repays 25% of the shareholder loan and calls part of the guarantee/tax exposure. This is an explicit joint stress, not a claim that all liabilities will crystallise. Base and bull cases require more growth funding, so their maximum cash gap can exceed the bear’s: faster sales are not free cash.

The most important falsifier of a recovery thesis is failure to convert the large connected receivable and capital advances into collected cash or productive assets without fresh adverse funding. The strongest evidence against a wholly pessimistic interpretation is real operating history, positive profits, a genuine RINL order, an upgraded cooperative CRISIL status and the auditor’s no-current-default conclusion. These could support recovery if liquidity and collections are demonstrated. Conversely, the 2018 OTS ₹40 crore waiver evidences historical lender loss but is not current insolvency. A cash-reserve assumption or hypothetical funding gap must not be presented as a factual default.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A five- or ten-bagger is speculative/unsupported on the present evidence. Over the 1,826-day horizon,5× requires about 38% annual price appreciation and 10× about 58.5%, before considering trading costs. Business growth, enterprise value, equity value and per-share return are different: debt claims, growth capital and dilution can absorb enterprise growth.

A simple decomposition would require revenue expansion, sustainable owner net margins and an acceptable exit multiple, multiplied by the fraction of current ownership retained after issuance. Current history does not establish this combination. Manufacturing revenue has declined, incremental capital returns are low, and the IPO did not eliminate working-capital dependence. A policy benefit or capacity approval alone cannot fill those gaps.

The model’s bull case combines 20% manufacturing volume growth,2% price growth,17% manufacturing EBITDA margin,40% incremental WC and a 9 times terminal EBITDA valuation, yet still requires prefunded hypothetical equity. Its per-share result is far short of 5×. A substantially faster path would require more ovens, qualified customers, coal supply, cash conversion and financing than currently evidenced. No precise success probability or promotional target is assigned. A multibagger claim would become researchable only after measured volumes, attractive mature incremental returns and a financeable per-share growth bridge replace the present assumptions.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Connected collections: baseline Om Avi receivable ₹20.0108 crore at 31 March 2026. Seek a full opening-to-closing sales/advance/cash reconciliation and subsequent receipts in the next audited/interim disclosure. No movement despite continued sales is an alert; verified impairment or concealment would materially change governance and downside conclusions.
2. IPO use: reconcile ₹1.1428 crore net-proceeds/expense difference and the explicit auditor deviation. Track ₹7.6213 crore remaining object allocation, including ₹4.1978 crore bank earmark and ₹3.4235 crore temporarily used in WC. Repeated contradictory reporting is a warning; proven non-business diversion is a thesis break.
3. Funding: establish current unrestricted cash, sanctioned undrawn limits and ₹20.4337 crore shareholder-loan terms before valuation is activated. Shareholder authority is not a facility. Unfinanced compulsory repayment is a survival warning.
4. Manufacturing economics: publish FY26/FY27 tonnes, realised prices and utilisation on a consistent capacity basis. Recovery must improve value added and cash, not only gross trading revenue.
5. Capital execution: obtain commissioned capacity/date, vendor advances converted to assets and funded cost-to-complete. Consent without output is not completion.
6. Cash quality: seek positive post-interest cash after recurring reinvestment across more than one reporting period; distinguish advance capitalization from cash recovery.
7. Audit closure: verify GSTR 1 amendments, gratuity valuation, IPO/CARO corrections and current RPT disclosures, retaining favourable bank-return/no-default evidence.
8. Policy and implementation: check actual applicable ADD exemptions/customer mix, BSE 20/60 session turnover, lot, circuits, surveillance and depth at the intended trade date. These are research review triggers, not automatic monitoring subscriptions.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved. It is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate and is excluded from quality, growth-quality and investment rankings pending material reconciliation. The business may recover, but current evidence does not support treating policy protection, capacity expansion or positive reported PAT as durable intrinsic-value-per-share compounding.

The decision sequence is specific. First reconcile the connected receivable, IPO utilisation/net proceeds and audit contradictions. Second establish current cash, restricted balances, debt terms and funded remaining commitments. Third authenticate the BSE cutoff/reference price and implementation data. Only then rebuild a supported base case and compute R/P/L and IAS. The business-quality score can also become complete only when balance-sheet resilience is scoreable.

Do not buy merely because the market capitalisation is small, and do not short or assume insolvency because a conditional cash model shows a gap. GOV 4 is below an adequate stewardship assessment but above the severe override threshold on the present evidence. New evidence of abuse would trigger that override; verified corrections and collections could improve the assessment. A lower share price alone would not fix G 2/G3 holds, although it could improve future price-dependent returns after those holds clear. No portfolio allocation, transaction or guaranteed fair value is proposed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary coverage includes the complete FY26 issuer annual report and BSE-filed mirror, final IPO prospectus with FY23–25 restated accounts, original FY22 audited consolidated accounts and comparatives, both dated rating rationales, complete IPO utilisation certificates, expansion consent, order disclosure, AGM notices/proceedings and the official policy annexure. Full audit/CARO/IFC/audit-trail sections were read, not inferred from the main opinion. Scanned financial and IPO audit pages were visually checked. Sources carry URLs, dates, hashes and locators; originals and personal identifiers are not included in the deliverable.

Source-safe reconstruction reproduces calculations from cited factual extracts; it does not re-authenticate missing original documents or manufacture current market evidence. Historical units are consistently converted to INR crore. Normalised 25% tax, manufacturing growth/margins, maintenance/growth reinvestment, reserve, repayment timing, contingent calls and hypothetical rescue terms are analytical assumptions. They are not management guidance or known funding commitments. The financial statements report FY26 EPS using year-end shares; no fabricated time-weighted denominator is supplied without an authenticated allotment date.

Open questions are material: collection/terms of Om Avi balances; the IPO expense and deviation bridges; exact supplier capital-advance allocation and project cost/commissioning; later cash and shareholder-loan terms; closure of audit other matters; actual manufacturing tonnes/prices and RINL execution; authenticated BSE price, surveillance and 20/60 session implementation data. Unknowns remain null or explicitly labelled ND/NS. Neither cash, debt, tax, prepaid capex nor operating property is counted twice in valuation.

summary:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability, funding and tradeability. This is a cyclical coke manufacturer with trading exposure, not an evidence-backed compounder. A domestic policy tailwind and a genuine RINL order create recovery possibilities, but they do not outweigh declining core manufacturing, weak incremental returns and poor cash conversion.

The decisive distinction is between reported cash and usable liquidity. At 31 March 2026, ₹5.3933 crore cash included ₹4.1978 crore earmarked IPO money and ₹1.1207 crore LC margin. Only ₹0.0748 crore remains after those labels. At the same date, one related-party receivable was ₹20.0108 crore, almost half total receivables. Recoverability and the bridge from sales/advances to that balance need evidence, not an assumed write-off or collection.

BQS and IAS are NS because balance-sheet/current-financing and price/implementation inputs are materially missing. GQS is 2.4/10, with the persistent weak-cash/capital-return ceiling of 5 explicitly applicable. No factor is filled with 5 merely to complete a score. Ordinary returns and entry prices are suppressed. Hypothetical prefunded rescue cases are diagnostic only. Positive audit findings and the absence of a current-year default are preserved; neither the 2018 OTS nor an issuer-noncooperation rating is called a current default.
